plan: OpenVibe.Shoes: every shoe, every market, the right price — one page per model with every store's all-in price, Shoes' own daily price snapshots, the size-price curve, cited specs, a price watch at a size and paste-a-link tracking through OpenVibe.Watch, and official drops with a reminder on Today
summary: OpenVibe.Shoes is the network's shoe resource. It reads OpenVibe.Deals' public offers (and the official eBay Browse API when a key pair is set), keeps the footwear in its own catalogue, and shows one page per model with every store's all-in price, a price history from its own one-snapshot-per-offer-per-day record, the size-price curve where sizes are known, and specs/fit/release/care only from cited open sources. A signed-in person can ask Watch to tell them when the model drops below a price at their size, or paste any listing link and have Watch apply its own fetch rules. Official release dates come from the brands' and stores' own public release pages; a reminder goes on Today. Shoes never enters a raffle, never scrapes Marketplace and carries no affiliate links.
works: Models and offers with a unique slug, all-in price, list price, condition, size, colourway, source check time and stale flag
One snapshot per offer per day (the first check wins), the price history and the size-price curve from those snapshots
The offers job over OpenVibe.Deals' public API, with the footwear classifier and product brand lookup
The drops job over a brand's or store's own release page, plus optional RSS feeds; every release cited and dated
A price watch at a size and a pasted listing link through OpenVibe.Watch's API with the person's own Network token
A drop reminder on OpenVibe.Today with the person's own token; no automated raffle entries
The public API: search with facets, one model with offers/history/curve/facts, the price a Watch polls, drops, the person's watches, source status, OpenAPI 3.1
The home via sc.room: hero, proof, biggest price drops today, dropping this week, popular models, three scenes, explore, developers, FAQ, network
Server-rendered pages, discovery artifacts, cache headers, account export/deletion and deploy files
Tests on PGlite and PostgreSQL: pure rules, the catalogue, the job parsers, every HTTP route
notYet: eBay is off until the host sets SHOES_EBAY_CLIENT_ID and SHOES_EBAY_CLIENT_SECRET
A watch needs the person's own Network token; a session without one saves it on Shoes and marks it not_connected
Specs, fit notes and care notes are empty until a cited open source is added to the shoe_facts table; the pages say not known yet
The size-price curve is empty until a source states the size; no size is invented
No closet, image search or merchant inventory feed (plan v2/v3)
The drops parser knows the Nike SNKRS launch payload and plain RSS; other calendars need their own parser
features: cited facts or not known yet
deployment: not deployed: the unit and nginx vhost are deploy/systemd/openvibe-shoes.service and deploy/nginx/open.shoes.conf
